newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 13.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 13.6 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 13.6 percent of its average daily volume of 538.1 million shares, or 73.1 million shares a day, for the week of August 4-8.
Of the average 73.1 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 36.9 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 36.2 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 86.7 million shares a day during the week of August 4-8.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities, Interactive Brokers, Susquehanna Brokerage Services and Natwest executed all of their program activity for customers.
Morgan Stanley split its program activity between that of its own account and those of its customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 79.5 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 19.7 percent of program volume from August 4-8.

Between August 4 and August 8, 14.9 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 0.5 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
